extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/authors submitting papers to the NeurIPS conference (machine learning community)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for completing the NeurIPS Paper Checklist that authors must submit with NeurIPS conference papers, covering reproducibility, transparency, ethics, and societal impact. Specifies format, question-response conventions, and 16 concrete checklist items authors should address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist presence and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The checklist promotes responsible ML research by addressing reproducibility, transparency, ethics, and societal impact. Papers lacking the checklist face desk rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must include the checklist with their submission; omission can lead to desk rejection. The checklist's purpose is to encourage responsible practices across submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Format Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must include in order: (1) submitted paper, (2) optional technical appendices, (3) NeurIPS checklist. The checklist doesn't count toward page limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the required ordering exactly. The checklist is appended after paper and appendices and will not be charged against page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Instructions for answering checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: For each question, answer: yes, no, or n/a (not applicable/not available). Authors may explain answers with brief 1-2 sentence justifications. Checklist responses are visible to reviewers and published with final papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep any explanatory justification concise (1-2 sentences). Be aware that reviewers and the public will see checklist answers, so maintain anonymization where required and be honest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Main claims in abstract and introduction must accurately reflect contributions and match experimental results regarding generalization scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure claims are neither overstated nor disconnected from empirical/theoretical evidence; explicitly match the stated scope of generalization to what experiments/theory demonstrate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should include a dedicated limitations section addressing strong assumptions, robustness to assumption violations, scope constraints, and performance factors. Authors shouldn't fear honest limitation disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss strong modelling assumptions, where methods may fail, sensitivity to distributional shifts, and other limitations; a frank limitations section is encouraged and not penalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory, Assumptions and Proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: If including theoretical results, state all assumptions clearly and provide complete proofs (main paper or supplemental). Include proof sketches for intuition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either include full proofs in the supplement or provide complete proofs in the paper; include a sketch in the main text for intuition. Explicitly enumerate assumptions used in theorems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental Result Reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide reasonable reproducibility avenues appropriate to contribution type—whether through algorithm clarity, architecture description, model access, or detailed replication instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose reproducibility artifacts suitable to the contribution: pseudocode/algorithms for algorithmic work, architectures and training recipes for model work, or runnable models and exact replication scripts when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Access to Data and Code
rubrics_metrics.description: Include code, data, and instructions for reproducing main experimental results (supplemental or URL). While encouraged, non-inclusion isn't grounds for rejection unless central to contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide URLs or supplemental materials for code and data when possible. If code/data cannot be shared, explain constraints; if reproducibility is central to the claim, lack of access may be more consequential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental Setting/Details
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify all training details including data splits and hyperparameter selection. Important details belong in main paper; full details can reside in code or supplements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report dataset splits, preprocessing, hyperparameter search procedures and chosen values, random seeds, training/validation/test protocols; put essential details in the main text and exhaustive settings in supplements or code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiment Statistical Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Report error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests for main claims. Clearly state variability factors and calculation methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include measures of variance (e.g., standard deviation over seeds, confidence intervals) and describe how they were computed; justify statistical testing choices where used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiments Compute Resource
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose computer resources needed (CPU/GPU type, memory, execution time) for reproducing experiments, including total compute estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report hardware types (GPU/CPU models), memory, wall-clock times, and estimated total compute (e.g., GPU-hours) required to train/evaluate models to reproduce main results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code Of Ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm adherence to 'NeurIPS Code of Ethics' and explain any necessary deviations while maintaining anonymity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State compliance with the Code of Ethics; if deviating, explain the deviation and mitigation while preserving author anonymity as required by the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss potential negative societal impacts when applicable—malicious uses, fairness concerns, privacy/security risks, and mitigation strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider and describe how the work might be misused or have unintended social consequences, discuss fairness and privacy implications, and propose mitigation strategies where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement safeguards for high-risk model releases requiring controlled access. Make good-faith efforts toward responsible release mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For models with high-risk potential, plan and describe access controls, rate limits, or staged releases; document efforts to responsibly release or restrict access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite creators and respect licenses for existing assets (code, data, models). Include URLs, version numbers, and license names (e.g., CC-BY 4.0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using third-party assets, provide attribution, precise references (URLs and versions), and state the license terms under which those assets are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assets (newly released)
rubrics_metrics.description: Document newly released assets with structured templates covering training details, limitations, licensing, and consent information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When releasing datasets, models, or code, supply metadata and documentation: training procedures, known limitations, license terms, and statements about consent/permissions where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crowdsourcing and Research with Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Include participant instructions, screenshots, and compensation details. Pay workers at minimum wage per Code of Ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the exact instructions shown to participants, interface screenshots, and describe compensation. Follow the Code of Ethics regarding fair payment (e.g., at least minimum wage).

rubrics_metrics.name: IRB Approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain Institutional Review Board approval when required for human subjects research. Clearly state approval status without breaking anonymity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If IRB approval was required, state whether it was obtained or is pending; report approval identifiers or statements in a way that preserves author anonymity during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of LLM usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe LLM usage only if it's an important, original, or non-standard core methodology component—not required for writing/editing purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not declare routine writing/editing use of LLMs; only describe use when the LLM is a substantive part of the method or experimental setup and detail how it was used.
